title: TRIM29 drives ulcerative colitis by disrupting lipid metabolism via lysosomal dysfunction: a multi-omics and experimental study.
authors: Guo, Xing-Zhou; Zhang, Lu-Yun; Tan, Zong-Biao; He, Hao-Dong; Liu, Ya-Fei; Yu, Bao-Ping; Dong, Wei-Guo
one_liner_zh: 该研究聚焦溃疡性结肠炎中TRIM29通过溶酶体功能障碍调控脂代谢的机制，未涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、转录因子结合或AI/物理模拟建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: The pathogenesis of ulcerative colitis (UC) involves genetic susceptibility and immune dysregulation. However, a more comprehensive understanding of its underlying mechanisms is still required. METHODS: Weighted correlation network analysis (WGCNA) and Mendelian randomization (MR) were used to investigate the association and causality between lipid metabolism and UC. Hub genes were identified by applying ensemble machine learning (LASSO, SVM, XGBoost) to the merged transcriptomic data, followed by cell-type-specific localization using public single-cell RNA-seq data from UC tissues. Pathophysiological relevance was confirmed in a DSS-induced colitis mouse model. The mechanistic role of the key hub gene was defined through knockdown LPS challenge in colonic epithelial cells, coupled with transcriptomic profiling. RESULTS: Integrated WGCNA and MR analyses established a strong association between UC and lipid metabolic pathways, which was experimentally confirmed by marked intracellular lipid accumulation in UC models. Mechanistically, this dysregulation was traced to lysosomal dysfunction, a finding solidified by pharmacological modulation with Rapamycin (enhancer) and Chloroquine (inhibitor), which directly demonstrated that lysosomal activity governs lipid metabolic disturbance. Subsequent machine-learning-based feature selection from lysosome-related genes pinpointed TRIM29 as a central regulator. Functional and transcriptomic analyses together demonstrated that TRIM29 knockdown attenuates UC progression by rescuing the lysosome-lipid metabolism axis, as evidenced by restored lysosomal function, enhanced cytoskeletal transport, improved lipid catabolism, a resolved pro-inflammatory immune profile, and downregulated inflammatory signaling. CONCLUSION: This study identifies TRIM29 as a master regulator that drives UC progression by disrupting lysosomal function and reprogramming lipid metabolism. Our work delineates the TRIM29-lysosome-lipid metabolism axis, providing a mechanistic rationale for targeting TRIM29 as a promising therapeutic strategy in UC.
abstract_zh: 背景：溃疡性结肠炎（UC）的发病机制涉及遗传易感性和免疫失调。然而，仍需对其潜在机制进行更全面的理解。方法：采用加权相关网络分析（WGCNA）和孟德尔随机化（MR）研究脂质代谢与UC之间的关联性和因果性。通过将集成机器学习（LASSO、SVM、XGBoost）应用于合并的转录组数据鉴定核心基因，随后利用UC组织的公共单细胞RNA-seq数据进行细胞类型特异性定位。在DSS诱导的结肠炎小鼠模型中确认了病理生理相关性。通过结肠上皮细胞中的敲低LPS挑战结合转录组分析，明确了关键核心基因的机制作用。结果：整合WGCNA和MR分析确立了UC与脂质代谢途径之间的强关联，并通过UC模型中显著的细胞内脂质积累在实验上得到证实。机制上，这种失调被追溯到溶酶体功能障碍，这一发现通过雷帕霉素（增强剂）和氯喹（抑制剂）的药理学调节得到巩固，直接证明溶酶体活性控制脂质代谢紊乱。随后基于机器学习的溶酶体相关基因特征选择将TRIM29确定为核心调节因子。功能和转录组分析共同表明，TRIM29敲低通过挽救溶酶体-脂质代谢轴来减轻UC进展，证据包括恢复的溶酶体功能、增强的细胞骨架运输、改善的脂质分解代谢、消退的促炎免疫谱以及下调的炎症信号传导。结论：本研究将TRIM29确定为通过破坏溶酶体功能和重编程脂质代谢驱动UC进展的主调节因子。我们的工作描绘了TRIM29-溶酶体-脂质代谢轴，为靶向TRIM29作为UC中有前景的治疗策略提供了机制依据。
